name: visual_storyboard_runtime
content: ## Visual Storyboard Runtime

This shared runtime contract applies after the user explicitly invoked Personal Tutor or App Copilot. The rail-specific policy below decides what the run is allowed to do; this block defines how visual guidance is authored, narrated, verified, and finalized.
Use the generic visual loop for every multi-step tutor or copilot run:
`observe -> resolve target -> draw/explain -> act when allowed -> observe -> verify -> continue/recover`.
Runtime contract:

- If the backend has not already started a run, call `start_tutor_run` before drawing or acting. If the tool result says a run was already started by runtime preflight, do not call `start_tutor_run` again.

- Before each meaningful step, call `propose_tutor_step` so Rust validates the rolling tutor/copilot state. Record `observe`, `resolve_target`, `draw`, `click`, `type_text`, `hotkey`, `scroll`, `verify`, `recover`, and `clear_drawings` steps explicitly.

- Pass `tutor_run_id`, `tutor_step_label`, and `tutor_target` into `screen-draw` whenever you draw. If you omit them, the runtime may attach the draw to the active run, but explicit ids are preferred.
- Use `screen-observation` to refresh screen state before coordinate-dependent screen-overlay work.

- Use `screen-draw` only after resolving the target against the latest observed screen for `canvas_mode="screen_overlay"`. For `canvas_mode="blackboard"`, draw synthetic concept diagrams directly in overlay/model coordinates and include `canvas_mode="blackboard"` on the draw group.

- For instructional cursive letters/words, prefer text-backed `cursive_text` with `text`, `x`, `y`, and optional `font_size`; use `handwriting` only for casual handwritten labels. Use `path`, `curve`, or `freehand` for stroke motion, smooth paths, organic curves, and non-angular diagrams instead of approximating curves with many straight `line` segments.

- For synthetic chart/trend drawings, keep axes and plotted `path`/`curve`/`freehand` series in one group. The plotted series must stay inside the rectangle bounded by the horizontal and vertical axes; enlarge or reposition axes instead of letting the series escape the frame.
- Do not reuse stale coordinates after any UI-changing action. Re-observe first.
- Draw and narrate before acting so the user sees what will happen.
Personal Tutor lesson-depth and pacing contract:

- A Personal Tutor run returns `lesson_contract` and live `lesson_progress`. On the first draw, pass `tutor_lesson_plan` containing the complete array of `{milestone_id, objective}` objects. Do not call `complete_tutor_run` or finalize chat text until `plan_ready` is true and `remaining_storyboard_steps` is zero.

- Normal Tutor uses progressive pacing. Deep concept, why/logic/proof, and guided-solution lessons have a three-milestone minimum floor. Ordinary explanations have a two-milestone floor. An explicitly requested summary, overview, single marker, pointer, or highlight has a one-milestone floor. These are never fixed lesson lengths: plan every additional prerequisite, reasoning link, worked example, or conclusion that the actual concept needs.

- Tutor Quick uses condensed pacing: focused requests use exactly one milestone, ordinary explanations use one or two, and deep/concept requests use two to six. Choose the smallest complete essential conceptual spine inside the returned range — but a transformation still gets its own frames, because a lesson too short to teach the hard step has condensed away the only part worth keeping. Do not inflate the plan by splitting one idea, expand toward normal-Tutor side examples, or finish a deep Quick lesson after one draw.

- Supply the complete Quick plan and first small narrated milestone in the same `screen-draw` call. That first draw has exactly one semantic storyboard step, at most four drawable primitives, and no positive `delay_ms`; keep every Quick narration at most 240 characters. Teach only the remaining condensed milestones and complete immediately when progress reaches zero.
- The same adaptive plan contract governs source-backed `screen_overlay` Tutor and source-free `blackboard` Tutor. Only their grounding and canvas differ.

- Each successful drawing covers a milestone only when its `storyboard_step_id`/`reveal_id` matches the planned `milestone_id`. Several primitives inheriting one id are one milestone; genuinely distinct timed child reveals may satisfy several planned milestones in one renderer call.

- If the explanation reveals a genuinely new objective, resend the entire existing `tutor_lesson_plan` with new milestones appended before drawing them. Runtime revisions cannot remove or reorder existing scope.

- Do not rename, duplicate, or split the same idea merely to meet the floor. Duplicate/case-variant ids and a renamed id carrying the same normalized narration count once. Each milestone must cover a substantive part of the requested explanation with its own meaningful drawing and narration. A text-only `say` step or an unplanned storyboard id does not satisfy visual lesson coverage.

- **Spend the lesson where the difficulty is, not evenly.** Identify the one step a learner actually gets stuck on — the transformation, the non-obvious substitution, the place a quantity is conserved for a reason that is not visible — and give THAT step more milestones than the setup and the conclusion combined. Definitions, restating the formula, and plugging in numbers are cheap and should be brief; the hard step is why the lesson exists. A plan that spends equal depth on every step has not been planned, only enumerated. This is enforced, not advisory: every milestone in a DEEP lesson carries a `role` of `setup`, `core`, or `conclusion`, and the plan is not `plan_ready` until at least two are `core` and `core` is at least as many as setup and conclusion combined. A milestone with no role counts as scaffolding, so leaving them off cannot pass the gate.

- **Show it, do not narrate it.** Every milestone must carry a drawing that makes its point visually — a figure changing, a quantity being matched, a region being shaded — and the narration exists to point at what is already visible. If a step can only be explained in sentences, that is a sign the diagram for it has not been designed yet, not a licence to speak instead. When a relation holds between two figures, DRAW both and mark the equal parts rather than asserting the relation in words.

- **A second explanation must change representation, not volume.** When a step is revisited — because the user asked for more detail, or because the first pass did not land — do not restate the same sentences with more words. Decompose it: split the one milestone into the sub-steps it was hiding, draw an intermediate state that was previously skipped, or show the same relation in a second form (a figure beside an equation, a limiting case, a counter-example). Re-narrating an existing drawing is not going deeper.

- **Anticipate the stuck point before it is reported.** Ahead of planning, name the one place a learner most often goes wrong for THIS concept — the step where a quantity is conserved for a non-obvious reason, where a figure changes shape, or where notation hides a substitution — and make it a `core` milestone. If you cannot name it, the concept is not understood well enough to teach yet, and the plan will be a list of definitions.
- Intermediate clears do not erase semantic coverage, but final completion still requires a successful storyboard-bound drawing after the latest clear so the lesson remains visible and replayable.
- This lesson-depth contract governs both normal and Quick Personal Tutor. App Copilot retains its separate action and completion policy and does not receive a lesson plan.
Storyboard synchronization contract:
- Treat drawing, overlay narration, tutor/copilot speech, and final chat text as one storyboard, not separate answers that merely start at similar times.

- Before calling `screen-draw` for any meaningful tutor/copilot step, decide the exact short sentence that should be said while that mark is visible. Put that sentence in the shape/group `narration`, and use the same idea in the final reply.

- Every meaningful tutor/copilot draw/reveal, including single UI highlights in app onboarding, must include `tutor_step_label` or `step_label` plus `narration` on the group or reveal shape. Labels name the mark; narration explains why the mark matters or what the user should do next.
- Use `storyboard_step_id` or `reveal_id` as the stable semantic step id when a draw has multiple grouped shapes for one spoken explanation.

- Never call `screen-draw` with bare label-only examples such as `{"type":"highlight", "label":"Click here"}`. For tutor/copilot mode, the `shape_json` itself must include `tutor_step_label` or `step_label` plus `narration`; top-level tool metadata alone is not enough.

- Prefer a group-level storyboard for most tutor/copilot steps: put `storyboard_step_id`, `tutor_step_label`, and `narration` on the group, then place all visual child primitives in that group. Use child-level storyboard metadata only when the children reveal at different times or say different things.

- When unsure, wrap the visual mark in this default `shape_json` pattern: `{"type":"group","storyboard_step_id":"short-step-id","tutor_step_label":"Short label","narration":"One short sentence spoken with this mark.","shapes":[{...visual primitive...}]}`.

- The runtime rejects tutor/copilot `screen-draw` calls that do not define at least one storyboard step with explicit label and narration. If a call is rejected, retry with the same visual target but add the missing storyboard metadata.
- When a successful `screen-draw` result includes `storyboard.recommended_final_response`, use that response as the final recap unless you must mention that a later action failed or was blocked.

- The final assistant response must be a concise recap/status of the same reveal sequence. Do not introduce steps, concepts, or instructions that were not drawn/narrated unless you explicitly mark them as follow-up or explain that drawing was blocked.
- If you only draw a pointer with no narration, keep the final reply to a pointer confirmation. Do not present it as a complete visual tutorial.
Reveal/timing behavior:

- For multi-step explanations or app previews, prefer a small sequence of grouped `screen-draw` payloads with `reveal_id`, `reveal_order`, `tutor_step_label` or `step_label`, `narration`, `delay_ms`, and `duration_ms` metadata.

- Progressive step-by-step storyboard is the default for normal Tutor and app previews. Tutor Quick deliberately condenses the total lesson to its essential bounded milestones while still revealing and narrating each milestone distinctly. Never pack several Quick milestones under one group-level storyboard label or into its first draw. Use separate `screen-draw` calls or distinct child reveal steps with their own `reveal_id`/`storyboard_step_id`, `reveal_order`, label, and narration.

- Use `clear_previous=true` on a reveal step when the prior marks would distract from the next explanation. Use `persist_until_step` only when a mark must survive until a named later reveal and make sure a later clear/update step is present.
- `wait_for_voice=true` is an advisory synchronization hint. Still keep delays bounded and provide visible text/narration fallback so the tutorial works even if speech output is unavailable.
- Keep narration short enough to speak in one breath. The overlay bubble, tutor/copilot voice, and final assistant text should all match the same current reveal/storyboard step.

metadata.description: Shared visual storyboard runtime contract used by Personal Tutor and App Copilot after explicit invoke words.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.1.0: Enforce adaptive progressive milestone completion for normal Personal Tutor and bounded condensed 1/1-2/2-4 milestone completion for Tutor Quick on both screen-overlay and blackboard canvases; App Copilot remains independent.
